implementation_notes: In-process the idiomatic realization is a BackgroundService whose ExecuteAsync loops over a Channels reader and calls the service, resolving it from a scope per message; the loop is the endpoint and the endpoint class disappears. ReadAllAsync keeps the code linear while the channel handles hand-off and (in the bounded variant) backpressure. Prefer this form for in-process work queues and transports that expose no SDK of their own.
pitfalls: A scoped service such as a DbContext must not be captured by the singleton BackgroundService: resolve it from IServiceScopeFactory per message or state leaks across messages.
An unhandled exception in ExecuteAsync fails or stops the background task silently; catch per message and route the failure to the error path.
The default unbounded Channel<T> removes backpressure; use a bounded channel so producers feel a slow service.

variants.name: Broker SDK processor (Azure Service Bus ServiceBusProcessor)
variants.implementation_notes: With a real broker the SDK supplies the endpoint: subscribing a handler to ProcessMessageAsync delivers each received message to it, and the handler invokes the application service before explicitly completing, abandoning or dead-lettering the message - the acknowledgement boundary the in-process loop does not have. Use it whenever the transport is a queue or topic with its own delivery semantics; MassTransit and NServiceBus consumer classes are the equivalent shape with the framework owning retries.
pitfalls: The handler must not start or stop the processor from inside itself; the API documentation warns that this can deadlock.
Forgetting CompleteMessageAsync leaves the message to be redelivered after the lock expires, so the service runs again - at-least-once is the default, not a setting.
Letting an exception escape only increments the delivery count with no diagnosable cause; translate it into abandon or dead-letter explicitly.
